title: Build a one-year pro forma and compute additional financing needed (AFN) — Meridian Building Group
skillsReviewNote: `pro-forma` and `financial-forecasting` are NOT yet in docs/SKILL_TAXONOMY.md. Used here per the task; flagged for Codex to add to the taxonomy (CFO / forecasting domain) before freeze. `cash-forecasting` already exists.
scenario: You are the junior CFO at Meridian Building Group. Owner Jordan Reed wants to grow contract revenue 35% next year by taking on more work and buying additional equipment (the company is operating near capacity, so operating assets scale with sales). Build a one-year pro forma income statement and balance sheet using the percent-of-sales method, compute External / Additional Financing Needed (AFN), compute the sustainable growth rate, then explain the funding gap to the lender and stress-test the growth and margin assumptions. The base year is MBG's Q1-2026-annualized figures: contract revenue $4,430,000, net income $173,800, ending equity $619,084. Assume a 20% dividend/distribution payout (80% retention) and a flat 21% tax rate.

exhibits.title: Base-year figures (treated as annual)
exhibits.body: Sales (contract revenue) 4,430,000; cost of contract revenue 3,700,000; G&A 360,000; depreciation 80,000 (fixed); interest 70,000 (fixed); pretax 220,000; tax @21% 46,200; net income 173,800. Profit margin = 173,800/4,430,000 = 3.9233%.

exhibits.title: Base-year ending balance sheet (operating assets/liabilities scale with sales)
exhibits.body: Operating assets that scale: cash 642,300; AR 1,180,000; retainage receivable 295,000; contract asset 120,000; prepaid 85,000; net PP&E 1,430,000 (company at capacity → PP&E scales). Spontaneous (no-cost) liabilities that scale: AP 865,000; retainage payable 210,000; accrued payroll & burden 148,216; contract liability 310,000. Financing (non-spontaneous) items held flat unless AFN is added: line of credit 300,000; current portion LTD 180,000; long-term debt 1,120,000; common stock 100,000; ending retained earnings 519,084.

exhibits.title: Forecast assumptions
exhibits.body: Sales growth g = 35%. Payout 20% (retention b = 0.80). Variable items (cost of contract revenue, G&A) scale with sales; depreciation and interest held fixed. Tax 21%.

tasks.prompt: Project the income statement: cost of contract revenue and G&A scale with sales; hold depreciation (80,000) and interest (70,000) fixed. Compute projected operating income, pretax income, tax (21%), and net income.
Compute the projected addition to retained earnings (net income × retention 0.80) and projected dividends/distributions (× 0.20).
Project total operating assets at 35% growth (every operating asset scales with sales): cash, AR, retainage receivable, contract asset, prepaid, net PP&E. Give the projected total assets.

Compute the spontaneous financing generated: (a) projected spontaneous liabilities (AP, retainage payable, accrued payroll, contract liability — all scale ×1.35), plus (b) existing financing liabilities held flat (LOC 300,000 + CPLTD 180,000 + LTD 1,120,000), plus (c) projected equity (common stock 100,000 + ending RE 519,084 + addition to RE 220,884). Give the total financing available before any AFN.
Compute External / Additional Financing Needed (AFN) = projected total assets − financing available before AFN.
tasks.explanation: AFN = 5,065,605 − 4,509,809.60 = 555,795.40. Even though MBG is profitable, asset growth of $1,313,305 outpaces spontaneous liabilities (+$536,625.60) plus retained earnings (+$220,884), leaving a $555,795 funding gap that must come from outside financing (LOC draw, term debt, or owner capital).

tasks.prompt: Compute the sustainable growth rate g* = (ROE × retention) ÷ (1 − ROE × retention), using base ROE = net income 173,800 ÷ ending equity 619,084 and retention 0.80.
tasks.explanation: ROE = 173,800/619,084 = 0.280737. ROE×b = 0.280737×0.80 = 0.224590. g* = 0.224590/(1−0.224590) = 0.224590/0.775410 = 0.289640 (≈28.96%). The 35% growth target exceeds the 28.96% sustainable rate, which is exactly why external financing is required.

tasks.prompt: Stress-test: if sales growth is only 25% (not 35%), projected total assets = 3,752,300 × 1.25. Recompute AFN holding the same percent-of-sales relationships and 21% tax (net income at 25% growth = 251,773 → addition to RE 201,418; spontaneous liab × 1.25). Give the new AFN.
tasks.explanation: At 25%: sales 5,537,500; cost of rev 4,625,000; G&A 450,000; operating income 382,500; pretax 312,500; tax 65,625; net income 246,875; addition to RE (×0.80) 197,500. Projected assets 3,752,300×1.25 = 4,690,375. Spontaneous liab 1,533,216×1.25 = 1,916,520. Equity 100,000+519,084+197,500 = 816,584. Financing available = 1,916,520 + 1,600,000 + 816,584 = 4,333,104. AFN = 4,690,375 − 4,333,104 = 357,271. Versus $555,795 at 35% growth — lower growth materially shrinks the funding gap.
tasks.note: Directional teaching task: lower growth → smaller AFN. Codex: verify the relationship, not a penny-exact figure; tolerance intentionally wide.

gradingRules.writeup: keyword + correctness on the growth-vs-funding distinction

deliverables.name: Lender forecast narrative
deliverables.body: MBG projects 35% revenue growth to $5.98M with net income of $276,105 (4.62% margin). To support that volume the company must grow operating assets — receivables, contract assets, and equipment — by roughly $1.31M. Spontaneous liabilities and retained earnings fund about $757,500 of that, leaving an Additional Financing Need of $555,795. Because the 35% target exceeds our 28.96% sustainable growth rate, the gap is structural, not a sign of weak operations. We are requesting a $600,000 increase to the line of credit (or a term note) to bridge the working-capital and equipment build, repayable as the new jobs bill and collect.

conversationSim.prompt: Owner Jordan Reed asks: 'If we're profitable and netting $276,000 next year, why do we need to borrow $556,000? Where does the money go?' Draft a 4-6 sentence explanation of growth vs. funding.
conversationSim.modelAnswer: Profit and cash are not the same thing when you're growing fast. To do 35% more work we have to fund 35% more receivables, retainage, contract costs, and equipment — about $1.31M of new assets tied up before customers pay us. Spontaneous financing (vendor payables, accruals, billings ahead of cost) and our retained profit only cover about $757,500 of that. The remaining $556,000 is cash locked into the bigger pipeline, so it has to be financed externally until the jobs bill and collect. The cleaner way to see it: our sustainable growth rate is only ~29%, so any growth above that requires outside capital — even though every job is profitable.
